# AI Migrations

> Lessons from products migrated to another language or framework with AI, for anyone running a
> large project with AI agents.

**Unofficial. No company named here endorses or is affiliated with this project.** Company and
product names describe the subject of each case only. Summaries are in our own words and link to
their primary sources.

<!-- disclosure: generated by scripts/build.mjs -->
Disclosure: the cases and lessons are drafted by Claude, an Anthropic model, and reviewed by the maintainer. At least 16 of the 24 cases used Claude models or Claude Code (Bloomberg, Ping.gg, GitHub, Checkly, Intel, Bun, GitLab, Mindstone, Datadog, Lutz Leonhardt, PagerDuty, Ladybird, Christopher Chedeau, Spotify, Robert Marshall, Slack; 6 others leave the models unstated), and Anthropic owns Bun, the subject of one case. GitHub, Intel, Mindstone and Ping.gg also used other vendors' models; where a source compares outcomes by model, that is its author's own unaudited report, and no lesson ranks vendors.

## What it does

<!-- contents: generated by scripts/build.mjs -->
Now: 24 cases (Slack, Zalando, Airbnb, Google, Robert Marshall, Spotify, Christopher Chedeau, Ladybird, Uber, PagerDuty, Lutz Leonhardt, 1Password, Datadog, Mindstone, GitLab, Bun, Asana, Intel, Checkly, Temporal, Shopify, GitHub, Ping.gg, Bloomberg), 153 lessons on 16 aspect pages, and a checklist of 12 questions.
<!-- /contents -->

- **Cases** ([cases/](cases/)): one file per migration done with AI, from engineering posts,
  papers and official repositories. Each says what AI did, what rule-based tools and people did,
  how the result was checked, the numbers with their basis, and what went wrong, including what
  the source leaves out.
- **Lessons** ([lessons/](lessons/)): what the cases teach about large AI-driven work, by aspect
  (reviews, tests, orchestration, rollout, cost). The sources stay migrations; the lessons apply
  more widely.
- **Checklist** ([checklist.md](checklist.md)): questions a coding agent can measure on a
  repository before a migration, each with a check and the evidence behind it.
- **Pitfalls** ([pitfalls.md](pitfalls.md)): what the old stack does without being asked, by kind
  of move, and seams for moving in steps.
- **For agents** ([llms.txt](llms.txt)): how to use the collection and one line per lesson page;
  it points to the case index for choosing cases, so an agent reads only what it needs.

[index.md](index.md) lists everything. [log.md](log.md) records what each update covered.

## Try it

**No warranty.** Everything here is provided as is, without warranty, under [`LICENSE`](LICENSE) (scripts, MIT) and [`LICENSE-CONTENT.md`](LICENSE-CONTENT.md) (text, CC BY 4.0); the maintainer is not liable for what applying it changes. Read each proposal before you apply it, on a branch or with a backup; a threshold marked "ours" is the maintainer's own starting point, not a measured value.

Open your coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, …) in your project and pick one of two routes:

- [Planning a migration](#planning-a-migration): run the checklist on the project you are
  thinking of moving to another language, framework or major version.
- [Learning from the lessons](#learning-from-the-lessons): compare how AI agents work in any large
  project with what these migrations taught. Lessons tagged "Old system as oracle: no" are the
  place to start; each is still judged by its own words.

The checklist and the lessons guide your agent through what the cases show; they do not decide
for your project. In both routes, step 1 only reads your project and changes nothing: you get
numbered findings, each with options and their trade-offs (the agent may say which one the
measurements favour, labelled as its reading), and you choose for each: do an option, later, or
skip. Run step 1 in a fresh session and paste step 2 in that same session. Steps 2 to 4 are
optional; run each revisit in a fresh session. Every revisit reads
[corrections.md](corrections.md) first: what we published wrong, and how to repair it.

<!-- /corrections -->

### Planning a migration

#### Step 1: review

```text
Read https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/llms.txt and follow it. Run the checklist on this project: measure every question with its check; do not judge from memory. Before writing up a finding, read that question's guide. Report in the checklist's report format: each finding with its measurement and the cases behind it, the options for it with their trade-offs (and where the guide says it may not apply here), then the findings that bear on going ahead and the main risks they show. Label your own reading as yours; the choices are mine. Change nothing.
```

Before applying anything, check step 1's claims: a proposal can rest on a wrong reading of your
project.

#### Step 2: apply

Once you have chosen, paste this with your choices in its first sentence:

```text
Apply the options I chose: 1A and 3B; 2 and 4 later; skip 5. Do the work the way this project normally runs work (yourself, or by briefing workers). Before changing anything, write the record https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/docs/report-formats.md defines in docs/migration-review.md with each chosen proposal's baseline: how often its problem has happened so far, with the evidence. For each proposal, first state its "Check now" and its "Event that proves it"; it is applied when the check now passes (waiting for first use), proven only once later work shows the event. Give each row waiting for first use the owner (who looks for its event) and check-by date (when that event should have shown) I named, or propose them for me to confirm. Where I left a question of fact unanswered, assume the default the report states and record the assumption; a decision I left open (an approval, a change to a project rule) stays open. Then complete the record, with every finding, including the later and skipped ones and the corrections.md entries checked ("none listed" if it has none), and the newest entry of https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/log.md this review covered.
```

To take the options the agent's reading favoured, replace the first sentence with "Apply the
options your reading favoured; mark the rest later."

#### Step 3: revisit later

When the collection has grown (llms.txt names a newer log entry than your record) or after a few
weeks of work, run a revisit in a fresh session. It first reads [corrections.md](corrections.md)
and checks your project for each entry; then it stops if nothing is new or due; else it re-checks
the record against its baselines, then measures what is new since your record's log entry and
gives options for it. Paste:

```text
Read docs/migration-review.md, then read https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/corrections.md and follow it before anything else: for each entry, check this project as it says and give me what you found, with options for any fix; change nothing but the record's "Corrections checked:" line; with no entry, say so in one line. Write what you checked on the record's "Corrections checked:" line. Then read https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/llms.txt. Compare the log entry the record names (date and title) with the newest entry llms.txt names; if they match and no item is due for re-check (an item is due when it is waiting or open and the project has commits since the record's date, or when it is past its check-by date), tell me and stop. Else read https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/checklist.md and follow its revisit step. List first the rows waiting for first use whose check-by date has passed, with their owner. Re-check each applied item (skipped ones stay skipped unless I reopen them): rerun its "Check now" unchanged, look for its "Event that proves it" in the work since, compare with its baseline, and mark it exactly "proven", "still waiting", "stopped holding" or "not shown" (its event cannot be seen yet), with the numbers; in the record's Status column, "still waiting" and "not shown" stay "waiting for first use". For each log.md entry newer than the record's, read its changes/ file (the lesson IDs and checklist questions it added, changed or removed); open only those, and measure them; do not judge from memory. List the applied lessons a newer lesson now contradicts or supersedes, and the items whose lesson changed. Give options only for the new or changed ones, earlier "later" items, applied items that stopped holding and what that list found, each as options with their trade-offs, for me to choose do, later or skip; label your own reading as yours. Update the record in its existing layout (add the Owner and Check by columns if it lacks them) and name in it the newest log.md entry you read, by date and title. Change nothing else until I choose.
```

#### Step 4: share what you learned (optional)

A [field report](docs/field-reports.md) says which questions foresaw the problems you hit and
which missed them; it is how the checklist improves. Wait until an item has met its problem since
its baseline (proven, or stopped holding); until then the record says nothing has happened yet.
Nothing is posted until you say yes. Paste:

```text
Read https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/docs/field-reports.md and follow it. Draft a field report from docs/migration-review.md, scrub it, and show me the exact text before posting. If no item has met its problem since its baseline, write that in the record with the date and do not draft a field report yet.
```

### Learning from the lessons

#### Step 1: compare

```text
Read https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/llms.txt and follow its route for large AI-driven work that is not a migration, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/docs/applying-lessons.md. Compare the lessons with how this project's agents and sessions work today; measure from the repository and its history, do not judge from memory. Report in that page's report format: numbered findings, each with the lesson ID, what the project does now, the options with their trade-offs and costs (and where the lesson's "Against" line says it may not hold here), and the check that would prove each. Label your own reading as yours; the choices are mine. Change nothing.
```

project.

#### Step 4: share what you learned (optional)

A field report from this route says which lessons held in a project that is not a migration; it
tells us which lessons and "Old system as oracle" tags to re-check against their cases. Wait until
an item has met its problem since its baseline. Nothing is posted until you say yes. Paste:

```text
Read https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/docs/field-reports.md and follow it. Draft a field report from docs/ai-lessons-review.md, naming which lessons held and which did not, scrub it, and show me the exact text before posting. If no item has met its problem since its baseline, write that in the record with the date and do not draft a field report yet.
```

## Contributing

Corrections are welcome: a wrong number, a broken link, a summary that misreads its source. Open
an issue; see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) gives the scope, the
commands and the writing rules, and points to the case format and the other rules in `docs/`.
